memos.headline: Broad bounce off April lows separates relative-strength leaders (S04, S06) from laggards (S02, S09) — selectivity warranted as RSIs cluster near overbought
memos.body: I see a market that has rallied hard over four weeks, but the quality of that rally varies enormously across the universe. S04 and S06 stand out with positive 12-week and 26-week returns, prices well above both moving averages, and strong relative strength vs SPY — though RSIs of 76.7 and 71.8 respectively warn of near-term exhaustion. S10 and S07 have staged explosive 4-week recoveries (+33.4% and +20.2%) but remain in longer-term downtrends (26w returns of -7.0% and -15.2%), making them lower-conviction momentum plays that could stall at overhead resistance. S02 is in freefall — down 53.3% from its 52-week high with an RSI of 19.8 and catastrophic relative strength (-48.6% vs SPY over 4 weeks) — and I see no technical reason to step in front of that. S09 and S01 are the weakest of the non-broken names, both trading below their 200-day means with negative 4-week relative strength, suggesting dead money at best.

views.note: Strongest trend in the universe: +9.5% above 200d mean, +11.8% 12w relative strength vs SPY, only 2.8% off highs — I'd reassess on a close below the 50d mean (~396).
Cleanest uptrend with lowest volatility (ATR 1.92%), +13.2% above 200d mean and positive relative strength on all timeframes; would cut on a break below ~241 (200d mean area).
Massive +33.4% 4w bounce is impressive but 20% above 50d mean is extremely stretched and 26w return is still -7%; wait for a pullback toward the 50d mean (~113) before committing.
Strong 4w rally (+20.2%) recaptured the 50d mean but price sits right at the 200d mean and 26w return is -15.2%; needs to clear ~370 convincingly to confirm trend change.
Decent 4w bounce (+19.1%) and above both moving averages, but 12w return still -7.8% and relative strength vs SPY is negative on 12w; watching ~190 (50d mean) as support.
RSI 19.8, down 53% from highs, -45% below 200d mean with 6.7% daily ATR — this is a broken chart and catching this knife has no technical support; would reconsider only above ~400.
Below both moving averages, worst 4w relative strength among non-broken names (-11.7% vs SPY), and only +1.2% 4w return while the market surged; dead money until it reclaims ~113 (50d mean).
Below both moving averages with -17.2% 4w relative strength vs SPY despite a mild +3.6% 1w bounce; low ATR (1.66%) limits downside but also upside — no edge here.
Barely above 50d mean (+1.3%), still 6.6% below 200d mean, and 12w relative strength vs SPY is -11.4%; needs to reclaim ~226 (200d area) to turn constructive.
Modest bounce (+9.9% 4w) but still below 200d mean and 19.5% off highs with negative relative strength; would need a close above ~171 (200d mean) to get interested.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Lead on Earnings Power; S07 and S09 Flash Warning Signs on Margin Compression
memos.body: I screened the latest filings across the universe and the dispersion in earnings quality is striking. S10 posted 56.2% net margins on 77.9% YoY revenue growth with only $8.46B in total debt—the cleanest balance sheet and strongest operating leverage in the group. S05 delivered $34.54B in net income on $90.23B revenue (38.3% margin) with net income up 46% YoY and minimal debt of $14.79B, which is durable earnings power I'm willing to pay for. On the other end, S07 saw revenue decline 9.8% YoY and net income collapse 29.8% to $2.00B on a 14.1% margin burdened by $31.74B in debt—a classic cash-flow compression setup I want to avoid. S09 is similarly concerning: flat revenue (+0.1%), declining net income (-6.2%), and a thin 9.3% margin that leaves little room for error against $32.82B of debt.

views.note: 56.2% net margin, ~80% YoY revenue and earnings growth, and only $8.46B debt make this the highest-quality earnings stream in the universe; a sustained margin decline below 40% would change my view.
38.3% net margin with 46% YoY net income growth and a clean $14.79B debt load signals durable, expanding earnings power.
36.9% net margin and 17.7% YoY net income growth on $70B revenue with manageable $42.88B debt; I'd reassess if margin dips below 30%.
Revenue of $155.67B grew 8.6% and net income surged 64.2% YoY, but the 11.0% net margin is thin for the scale and $58.75B debt warrants monitoring.
Solid 26% margin on $95.36B revenue but only 5.1% top-line growth and $92.2B in debt suggest limited upside from here without re-acceleration.
32.3% margin is attractive but $407B in total debt (financial-sector leverage) makes earnings durability harder to underwrite; need to see credit quality data.
Flat revenue, 6.2% net income decline, and a 9.3% margin against $32.82B debt point to compressing cash flows—exactly what I refuse to pay for.
Revenue down 9.8%, net income down 29.8%, 14.1% margin eroding, and $31.74B debt—clear earnings deterioration with no visible inflection.
Revenue grew 9.8% to $109.58B but a 5.7% net margin and $81.27B debt with unavailable YoY net income comparison leave too many open questions.
19.1% margin is decent but revenue declined 2.1% YoY and net income was essentially flat; $24.25B debt is manageable but growth needs to resume.

memos.headline: Fed on Hold at 4.50% With Cooling Inflation and Softening Labor Market — Positioning for a Late-2025 Easing Cycle
memos.body: I see the macro regime as a prolonged pause transitioning toward easing: the fed funds upper bound has been flat at 4.50% for three months, yet is down 100bp year-over-year, while CPI is running at just 2.3% y/y — well-behaved and consistent with the Fed eventually resuming cuts. The unemployment rate at 4.2% has risen 30bp over the past year and 20bp in the last three months, signaling a gradual labor market softening that should keep the Fed's easing bias intact. The 10y-2y spread has steepened sharply (+86bp y/y to +0.49pp), confirming the curve is normalizing and the market is pricing in further front-end easing. I favor duration-sensitive growth and banks that benefit from a steeper curve, while remaining cautious on pure cyclicals given the labor softening; a surprise CPI print above 3% or a payrolls surge reversing the unemployment trend would force me to revisit this call.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth benefits from a pause-to-easing regime with benign 2.3% CPI and a steepening curve.
Banks gain from the 86bp y/y steepening in the 10y-2y spread improving net interest margins.
Staples offer defensive value but limited upside in a regime where easing expectations support risk assets.
Cyclicals face headwinds from rising unemployment (+30bp y/y) signaling demand softening.
Growth-oriented sector should benefit as stable rates and moderating inflation support valuation multiples.
Energy lacks a clear macro tailwind; softening demand indicators offset any supply-side support.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: S04 and S06 Positive Momentum vs. S02 and S08 Negative Tone
memos.body: I see a clear split in event-driven sentiment across the universe this cycle. S04 posted a +7.6% earnings-day reaction on 4/30, the strongest positive signal in the group, and with no subsequent negative filings the tone remains constructive. S06 similarly rallied +4.0% on its 4/11 earnings release with supportive Reg FD disclosure the same day. On the negative side, S02 suffered a brutal -22.4% drop on its 4/17 earnings, followed by two director departure filings in quick succession—this pattern of management churn on top of a sentiment shock suggests the narrative is still deteriorating and unlikely priced through. S08 dropped -3.7% on its 5/1 earnings and filed an 'Other Events' 8-K on 5/12 that could signal further negative developments; I lack conviction that the tone has bottomed there.

views.note: Strongest positive earnings reaction in the universe at +7.6% with no subsequent negative filings suggesting sustained positive tone.
Solid +4.0% earnings pop on 4/11 with concurrent Reg FD disclosure; subsequent Other Events filing on 4/22 is benign noise.
The -22.4% earnings shock combined with two director departure filings signals a deeply negative and still-evolving narrative.
Earnings-day -3.7% decline followed by an ambiguous Other Events filing on 5/12 leaves tone uncertain and tilted negative.
Earnings reaction of -3.7% on 4/24 despite a dividend announcement earlier in April; negative tone likely already priced but no catalyst for reversal.
Modest +1.7% earnings pop and steady stream of Other Events filings suggest stable-to-positive tone without crowding.
Muted +0.6% earnings reaction and multiple director changes create mixed signals; no clear directional tone shift.
Flat +0.4% earnings reaction and early-April director change are non-events from a sentiment perspective.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Doubles in Three Months While VIX Retreats — Structural Geopolitical Risk Remains Elevated
memos.body: I am struck by the divergence between the VIX at 17.83 (down 41% over one month) and the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index at 469 (up 104% over three months and 26% over one month). This tells me markets have priced out near-term tail risk but the underlying policy environment — likely driven by tariff escalation, export controls, and energy-security debates — remains structurally uncertain. WTI crude at $63.03 is down 11% over three months, suggesting demand-side concern or supply normalization, which eases energy-cost pressure but also signals weaker global activity expectations. HY OAS at 3.20% has tightened 89bp in a month, indicating credit markets are sanguine, yet the 3-month widening of 58bp reminds us the policy shock has not fully unwound. I have moderate conviction that names with heavy cross-border or China supply-chain exposure face ongoing headline risk, while domestically oriented or defense-adjacent names are better positioned until we see a concrete de-escalation in trade policy.

views.note: Four 8-K filings in three weeks suggest active corporate maneuvering, possibly supply-chain or regulatory adjustments; I lack detail to take a directional view but the elevated policy uncertainty warrants caution.
Three filings in April cluster around the period of sharpest policy-uncertainty rise; without content detail I stay neutral but flag potential tariff or export-control exposure.

Early-April 8-Ks coincide with the onset of the policy-uncertainty spike; with WTI down 11% over three months and uncertainty doubling, I see geopolitical headwinds for names potentially exposed to energy or trade disruption.
Multiple Reg FD and 8.01 filings suggest proactive investor communication amid uncertainty; the 104% 3-month surge in policy uncertainty keeps me sidelined until trade-policy clarity improves.

Recent 8-K activity through mid-May and the VIX retreat suggest the market is comfortable with near-term risk; if S07 is domestically oriented, the tightening HY OAS supports a cautious long, though a new tariff escalation would change my view.
Single 8-K on May 12 provides insufficient signal; elevated policy uncertainty index at 469 means I cannot take a directional stance without more clarity on the firm's geopolitical exposure.
